notes.meaning: The evil spirit shrieked and threw the boy into a violent convulsion as it came out, trying to cause maximum harm before leaving. The boy was left so limp and still on the ground that the crowd thought he had died. Satan often attacks most fiercely right when his power over someone is broken.

Jesus gently reached out, took the fallen boy by the hand, and lifted him up fully restored. Where the demon brought violence and weakness, Christ brought tender compassion and healing life. His personal touch reminds us that the Lord cares deeply for those who are suffering.

Once they were alone inside the house, the disciples asked Jesus why they had been unable to cast out the spirit. They had driven out demons in the past, so their failure here left them confused and humbled. Bringing our shortcomings directly to Christ is always the right way to learn from our mistakes.

Jesus explained that such deep-seated spiritual bondage requires earnest, faithful prayer. The disciples had failed because they relied on their own past abilities instead of living in fresh dependence on God. Difficult spiritual battles can only be won when we actively rely on the Lord rather than ourselves.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Early Greek manuscripts end the sentence with 'prayer,' indicating that the phrase 'and fasting' was likely added by later copyists.

notes.meaning: Jesus and His followers traveled quietly through Galilee along side roads, keeping away from the public eye. He did not want large crowds gathering to hinder their journey toward Jerusalem. He chose privacy so He could focus all His attention on preparing the Twelve.

Jesus used this private travel time to teach His disciples about His coming death and resurrection. He told them plainly that He would be handed over to sinful men, murdered, and raised back to life three days later. Even while predicting His darkest trial, He gave them hope by promising victory over the grave.

The disciples could not grasp what Jesus meant because they still expected the Messiah to set up a visible, earthly kingdom. They were also afraid to ask Him for an explanation, perhaps fearing a sharp rebuke or dreading the answer. Unbelief and fear often keep believers from seeking the truth God wants to give them.

Upon reaching their lodging in Capernaum, Jesus asked the disciples what they had been talking about on the road. He already knew the truth, but He asked so they would face their own selfish attitudes honestly. Christ holds us accountable for our private conversations and disputes.

The disciples said nothing at all because they were deeply ashamed of their road-side debate. While their Master was thinking about His coming sacrifice, they had been bickering over who would hold the highest position in His kingdom. Their embarrassed silence showed that their consciences knew their ambition was sinful.

Jesus sat down like a teacher delivering an essential lesson, called the Twelve close, and completely overturned worldly thinking. In God's kingdom, real greatness does not come from lording power over others, but from putting oneself last and serving everyone. The highest place in heaven belongs to those who gladly take the lowest seat on earth.

Jesus brought a little child into the middle of the group and then warmly gathered the child into His arms. Children held no status or social power in that culture, making this child the perfect picture of humble unimportance. Through this tender action, Jesus showed how deeply He values those whom the world overlooks.

Jesus taught that welcoming a lowly, humble believer for His sake is the very same thing as welcoming Him. Even more, receiving Christ means receiving God the Father who sent Him. Loving and serving the humblest Christian is one of the highest ways to show love to God.

John reported that the disciples had tried to stop a man from casting out demons in Jesus' name because he did not travel with their group. The disciples were acting out of jealousy, wanting to keep miracles and honor solely for their inner circle. We must never oppose genuine kingdom work just because someone does not belong to our particular group.

Jesus told His disciples to stop hindering the man. Anyone who has faith to work a miracle using Jesus' name is honoring Him and will not easily turn around and slander Him. Believers should rejoice whenever the power of evil is broken through the name of Christ.

Jesus gave a generous principle: anyone who is not working against His cause should be treated as an ally. While we must examine our own hearts strictly, we should treat others who serve Christ with broad charity. True Christian unity reaches far beyond our own narrow boundaries.

Jesus assured the disciples that even a simple cup of water given to someone because they belong to Christ will be rewarded. God notices every small kindness done out of love for His Son. No act of humble Christian service is ever forgotten by God.

Jesus gave a terrifying warning about causing humble believers to fall into sin or lose their faith. He stated that being drowned in the sea with a massive millstone tied around one's neck would be far better than facing God's judgment for harming a Christian's walk. We must be very careful that our pride or careless conduct never leads another believer astray.

Jesus urged His followers to take radical action against sin, comparing it to cutting off one's own hand. He did not mean physical self-mutilation, but ruthlessly putting to death sinful habits, actions, or relationships no matter how precious they seem. Entering eternal life through painful self-denial is far better than clinging to sin and ending up in hell.

Words from the prophet Isaiah describe the unending misery of the lost. The undying worm represents the painful, never-ending bite of a guilty conscience, while the unquenchable fire points to God's holy wrath against unrepentant sin. No earthly pleasure is worth the eternal ruin of the soul.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Early Greek manuscripts omit this verse, showing it was copied into this spot by later scribes from verse 48.

notes.meaning: Jesus repeated His warning using the foot, showing that believers must refuse to walk down paths or visit places that lead into sin. Just as a sick limb must be amputated to save a body, we must abandon dangerous freedoms to protect our eternal life. Faithfulness to God requires cutting off whatever draws our steps away from Him.

Repeating this solemn warning underscores how certain and terrible final punishment will be. The combined picture of gnawing worms and blazing fire shows a state of unending misery where the soul never ceases to suffer. God gives these warnings so that people will turn away from sin before it is too late.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Textual scholars point out that this verse is absent from the oldest manuscripts, having been added by scribes to mirror verse 48.

notes.meaning: Jesus warned that even our eyes can lead us into ruin through lust, greed, and envy, and must be plucked out in a spiritual sense. Believers must strictly guard what they look at and desire, cutting off all sinful sights and longings. Missing out on worldly pleasures is a tiny price to pay for entering God's kingdom.

Quoting Isaiah, Jesus gave a final description of hell as a place where the worm never dies and the fire is never put out. These vivid figures portray eternal separation from God, where remorse never fades and divine justice never ends. The terrifying reality of hell reminds us how dangerous and deadly sin truly is.

Under the law of Moses, every sacrifice had to be sprinkled with salt to make it acceptable to God. In a similar way, every disciple must be seasoned by the purifying fire of trials, discipline, and self-denial to be an acceptable living sacrifice. Those who refuse this painful work of grace in this life will instead face the destructive fire of judgment.

Salt is valuable because it preserves and adds good flavor, but if it loses its saltiness, it becomes entirely useless. Jesus urged His followers to keep the seasoning of God's grace and holy character active in their hearts. That inner grace would cure their selfish ambitions and produce true peace with one another.
